items.description:
The Italian Art Shop is an art materials supplier in Rondebosch, stocking a wide range of oil and acrylic paints for artists at different budgets. Its oil paint range includes Sennelier Artist Quality paints and oil sticks, Michael Harding, Divolo Accademia, several Maimeri ranges, Winsor and Newton Winton Oil, and Rublev Oils.

For acrylics, the shop stocks Maimeri Polycolor body acrylics, Sennelier Artist Quality and Abstract acrylics, Winsor and Newton Galeria acrylic, Maimeri Acrilico, and ready-made acrylic paint sets. The shop publishes price comparisons across its acrylic range so customers can choose paint to suit their budget, alongside painting mediums and additives.

It suits painters and art students who want to compare paint brands and prices before buying, from student-grade to professional artist-quality ranges.

The Marly Boutique Hotel and Spa is a five-star, 38-room hotel in Camps Bay, set between the curve of the Atlantic and the Twelve Apostles. The hotel is named after the Chateau de Marly, a leisure residence built for Louis XIV, and it positions itself as a destination in its own right rather than just a place to sleep.

Rooms and suites range from sea-facing and mountain-facing options to deluxe two-bedroom mountain suites, with sizes from 30 to 66 square metres. The hotel has a rooftop pool, a boutique spa and on-site luxury retail, and some of the city's top restaurants are just steps away.

Guests who book directly are offered the lowest available rate, flexible cancellation terms, and access to dedicated reservations specialists throughout their stay. It suits travellers who want a central, full-service base in one of Cape Town's most sought-after beachfront neighbourhoods.

Willoughby and Co is a Japanese fusion restaurant that has operated at the V&A Waterfront since 1996, led by head chef Sam and his team. Over nearly three decades the kitchen has introduced thousands of patrons to fusion-style Japanese cooking, offering a full Japanese menu that ranges from the freshest sushi to tempura dishes, oyster shooters, soups and salads.

The restaurant also runs a catering service for functions and events, preparing whole baked fish, platters of its well-known sushi, or fresh oysters for collection. Its wine shop staff are available for wine tastings to pair with a meal.

The restaurant is on the ground floor of Victoria Wharf at the V&A Waterfront, and it suits diners who want a long-established Japanese fusion menu, or who are planning catering for an event.

items.description:
Chamomile Farming is a family-run agricultural business established in 2003, farming 1.6 hectares and 22 hectares of land at Schaapkraal in the Philippi Horticultural Area on the outskirts of Cape Town. The Philippi Horticultural Area is one of the city's key urban farming belts, and small, family-run operations like this one form part of that food-growing landscape.

As a family business, Chamomile Farming has built its operation on land within Schaapkraal, working the same two plots of farming land for more than two decades. The business can be reached directly by phone or email for enquiries about its produce.

It suits buyers looking for crops grown on a small, family-run farm within the Philippi Horticultural Area rather than from a large commercial grower.

Collectables Hub and Cafe is an antique store and cafe at the top of a long, narrow staircase in Simon's Town, which opened in 2021. The two-storey space is packed with retro memorabilia, collectables and quirky statues, from aliens and dinosaurs to superheroes and an ostrich, with a bright yellow staircase and gates marking the entrance.

Upstairs, the cafe deck has a sea view over Simon's Town Harbour, giving visitors a spot for coffee after browsing the antiques below. A plastic concierge figure greets guests at the entrance with a sign promising awesome coffee and stunning views.

It suits collectors, thrifters and visitors to Simon's Town who want to browse unusual finds before having a coffee with a harbour view.

Freeline is a garment printing business based in Ndabeni, offering textile screen printing, sublimation, digital print, vinyl cut and transfer solutions. The company works on promotional printing for garments, positioning itself around free thinking, free style, free living and free spirited design approaches for clients.

The business is based at the Sunrise Building on Morningside Drive in Ndabeni, and it also runs Freeline Sport, a dedicated offering for sports-related printing and apparel. Its office is open on weekdays, with a shorter day on Fridays.

It suits businesses, sports clubs and individuals who need garments printed or branded through screen printing, sublimation or vinyl cutting.

items.description:
The Trevoyan Guesthouse is a boutique guest house in a Victorian residence dating back to 1896, tucked away in Tamboerskloof a short stroll from the city's bars and restaurants. The house has seven individually designed rooms and suites, a garden and a tranquil pool, with different bed sizes and coffee and tea facilities in each room.

Breakfast is made from fresh, local produce and served from a buffet that includes homemade granola, baked on site, along with a selection of breads, jams, marmalade and local cheeses. A popular summer option on the menu is a bowl of organic tomatoes with olive oil, feta and capers, or toasted rye with sliced avocado.

The guesthouse also has a Fiat 500 available for guests to explore the city in. It suits travellers who want a small, individually furnished guest house with a pool, within walking distance of Cape Town's city centre.

TSIBA Business School is part of a social enterprise that also includes the TSIBA Ignition Academy and an Education Trust, working to develop sought-after graduates and successful small businesses. The school recently relocated to a new campus, TSIBA House, at 51 Old Mill Road in Ndabeni, which it says enables far greater impact than its previous site.

Courses include a Higher Certificate in Business Administration, a Bachelor of Business Administration in Entrepreneurial Leadership, a Postgraduate Diploma in Business Administration, and a Diploma in ICT through the Cisco Networking Academy, alongside various short courses. The business school's stated mission is to invest in purpose-driven people and emerging businesses that lead social change, challenging the status quo of business education through a values-based approach.

The Ignition Academy side of TSIBA offers skills development and occupationally directed training for young people and entrepreneurs, aiming to close skills gaps and support small business growth. It suits students and aspiring entrepreneurs who want a business education grounded in social impact.

Two4One Kitchen and Bar is a restaurant on Lower Main Road in Observatory, built around what it calls the first restaurant concept of its kind in South Africa: every meal on the menu is available two for the price of one, all day, every day. The menu covers juicy burgers, topping-filled pizzas and cheesy chilli poppers, among other options.

Diners can mix and match two different menu items, with the lower-priced item served free, or swap the second meal for a draft beer or house drink instead of a second plate. As an example of the value on offer, a burger and chips costs R120, with a second burger and chips thrown in for free.

It suits groups and value-conscious diners in Observatory who want to share two meals, or trade a second plate for a drink, every day of the week.

Baker and McVeigh Equine Hospital in Milnerton was established in 2002 as a sister practice to Baker and McVeigh Summerveld, before being overhauled in 2006 into the fully equipped hospital seen today. The practice provides a comprehensive ambulatory service alongside a fully equipped and accredited equine hospital, serving racehorses, thoroughbred studs, sport horses, polo ponies and leisure horses across Cape Town and the surrounding areas.

Its hospital facilities include dedicated surgical suites and on-site surgeons offering emergency colic, respiratory tract, orthopaedic and soft tissue surgery, along with equine reproduction procedures for stallions and mares. The practice also offers complete dental care, including routine dental work, oroscopy and advanced extractions, as well as poor performance investigations and gastroscopy.

It suits horse owners who need specialist equine veterinary care, from routine dental work to emergency surgery, in the Cape Town area.

Belhar High School is a public, co-educational high school in the Cape Flats area of Belhar, serving 1,318 learners with a staff of 40 educators. The school delivers the National Senior Certificate curriculum under the CAPS framework, teaching in both Afrikaans and English, and recorded an 89.1% matric pass rate in 2025.

The school is not a no-fee institution and does not offer boarding facilities, and its culture is described as community-oriented, inclusive and sports-focused. Admissions at the school are open, following the standard process set out for public schools in the Western Cape.

It suits families in Belhar and the surrounding Cape Flats who want a dual-medium public high school with a strong recent matric pass record.

Club Kloof is an Italian-ish restaurant and bar at 84 Kloof Street, serving brunch, lunch, drinks and dinner from midday to late. The kitchen opens for lunch from midday and for dinner from 6pm, with both walk-ins and bookings through Dineplan accepted.

The venue runs Club Art, a collaborative project with local artists that creates a conversation between art, design and food, and it sells its own Club Merch, with some items made in-house and others sourced from friends, suited to gifts or for keeping. For bigger groups, the team offers a private room or a bigger table upstairs for events, available on request.

It suits diners who want Italian-inspired food and drinks with a side of local art and design on Kloof Street.

Guga S'thebe Arts and Culture Centre is a community arts hub in the heart of Langa, operating since 1990 on Washington Street, now often referred to as King Langalibalele Avenue. The centre features art studios for pottery and mosaics, a theatre built from recycled materials, and live drumming as part of its cultural programme.

Entrance to the centre is generally free, though costs may apply for specific shows, workshops or activities, which are often booked through platforms such as Quicket or Webtickets. Guided township tours that include a stop at Guga S'thebe are also available through various tour operators.

It suits visitors who want to see community art and performance in Langa, whether dropping in during the day or booking a specific show or workshop.

items.description:
Loaves by Madame Baker is a bakery and cafe in Salt River, founded in 2015 and known for its breads, coffee and freshly baked pastries made every morning. The business first opened its doors on Long Street in April 2015, under the name Loaves on Long, before relocating to Salt River in 2018.

The bakery's approach grew out of a passion for baking passed down through family, shaping an unwavering focus on producing the best quality product possible regardless of what is being made. The cafe offers single items as well as baking classes for those who want to learn the craft themselves.

It suits bread and coffee lovers in Salt River who want freshly baked pastries and a quality cup of coffee each morning.

Morkel and De Villiers Inc is a law firm that has been setting legal precedents in the Helderberg area since 1918, giving it more than a century of experience in the region. The firm runs a large conveyancing and litigation practice and is involved in every sphere of legal work, including commercial matters.

Its practice areas cover property law, estate law, commercial law and litigation law, with a team of qualified attorneys, conveyancers and notaries handling client matters. The firm publishes articles on topics such as real estate fraud, the costs of estate planning, and what happens after an accident, to help clients understand these areas.

It suits clients in the Helderberg area who need conveyancing, litigation, estate or commercial legal services from a long-established local firm.

items.description:
Pier is a fine dining seafood restaurant at the V&A Waterfront, rated 4.8 from 651 Google reviews and led by chef John Norris-Rogers. The restaurant offers an intimate multi-course tasting menu that the venue describes as the pinnacle of fine dining in Cape Town, with beautifully composed dishes that celebrate the ocean right at the iconic Pierhead.

The restaurant is in the Slipway Corner building on the ground level of the Pierhead District, next to the NSRI, with parking available at the Ulundi Parkade. It opens for lunch and dinner within set hours each day, and bookings are recommended given its reputation as a destination restaurant.

It suits couples and special-occasion diners looking for an elevated, ocean-focused tasting menu with harbour views.

Reverie Social Table is a pocket-sized, home-style restaurant on Lower Main Road in Observatory, built around an 18-seater table where guests from different walks of life sit down together to break bread. The concept has introduced locals and visitors, from Cape Town foodies to international tourists, to an evening of shared conversation over a meal.

The kitchen is led by a chef with experience at a well-known Franschhoek restaurant and two Michelin-starred restaurants in London and Paris, and the menu changes weekly to keep the food creative. A five-course meal is typically paired with wines from a boutique Franschhoek farm, with an elegant MCC served on arrival.

The restaurant includes a small library and courtyard as part of the space, and staff are known for presenting each course without disturbing the flow of conversation at the table. It suits diners who want a communal dining experience with strangers as much as a good meal.

Simon's Town Boat Company runs boat tours out of Simon's Town, operating two custom-designed vessels skippered by qualified crew. Every tour is accompanied by an expert commentary, giving passengers context on what they are seeing as they explore what the company calls the most beautiful bay in the world.

The company is based at 2 Wharf Street in Simon's Town, within walking distance of the harbour, making it an easy stop for visitors already exploring the town. Bookings and enquiries can be made directly through the company's contact details.

It suits visitors to Simon's Town who want a guided boat trip on False Bay with commentary included.

The Blue Cafe is a long-standing cafe in Tamboerskloof, trading since somewhere between the mid-1890s and the early 1900s, making it over a century old. Loved by locals, it has become a place where neighbours keep in touch with each other, as well as a spot to buy coffee, light meals and deli produce.

Over the generations the cafe has been owned by a few different families, each adding to its role as a neighbourhood fixture. One of its ongoing initiatives invites local parents to let their children harvest fruit and vegetables from their own gardens to sell to the cafe, encouraging a young entrepreneurial spirit in the area.

It suits Tamboerskloof locals who want a historic neighbourhood cafe for coffee, a light meal or deli produce.

The Village Vetshop at Plattekloof Village has been trading since 2005, combining convenient shopping with a professional yet friendly environment for pet owners. The shop is staffed by a trained team, and veterinarians are available on site to help clients with pet health questions where appropriate, under the shop's 'Passionate about Pets' approach.

Its product range covers veterinary counter-products such as tick and flea treatments, de-wormers, shampoos and supplements, along with veterinary-approved diets from brands including Hills, Royal Canin, Eukanuba and Iams. The shop also stocks beds, blankets and dog jerseys, homeopathic supplements for conditions such as stress and skin allergies, a range of toys and training aids, and runs an in-house loyalty card for regular customers.

A small deli within the shop rounds out the offering. It suits pet owners at Plattekloof Village who want veterinary advice alongside everyday pet supplies in one stop.

Uwe Koetter Jewellers is a South African jeweller creating bespoke engagement rings, wedding bands and fine jewellery in Cape Town since 1968. The business offers a Living Journey Collection alongside standard engagement ring ranges, and customers can design their own ring or commission a fully bespoke piece.

The jeweller also makes signets and family crests, giving clients a way to commission jewellery tied to their own family history rather than choosing from a standard catalogue. The business publishes guidance for customers, including how to give old, worn or dated jewellery a new life rather than replacing it, and notes on gemstones such as tanzanite, found only near Mount Kilimanjaro in Tanzania.

It suits couples and clients in De Waterkant who want a custom-designed ring or commissioned piece from a jeweller with decades of experience in Cape Town.

Vergenoegd Löw Wine Estate is a heritage wine farm near Stellenbosch, founded in 1696 and restored since 2015 across its Cape Dutch manor house, werf and farm buildings. The estate combines wine tastings, farm-to-table dining, a spa and accommodation on regeneratively farmed vineyards bordered by conserved wetlands.

Visitors exploring the werf before lunch are likely to encounter the estate's famous flock of Indian Runner ducks, kept for pest control among the vines, and Australorp chickens that forage in the vegetable garden, with both supplying eggs for the kitchen. The farm's two restaurants, Geuwels and Clara's Barn, serve food built around classic South African flavours and heartfelt, farm-to-table cooking.

It suits visitors who want a wine tasting, a farm-to-table meal or an overnight stay surrounded by birdlife and mountain views near Stellenbosch.

Anchor Industries is an industrial supplier in Ndabeni dealing in open link chain, steel wire rope, rigging hardware, slings and lashing equipment, material handling equipment, and ship's mooring and offshore mooring and towing equipment. The company's services extend beyond supply to equipment rental, wire rope services, rigging lofts and on-site marine services.

Its offering also covers component manufacturing, testing and inspection, and recertification of lifting and rigging equipment, giving marine and industrial clients a single supplier for both new equipment and ongoing compliance checks. The company describes its focus as reliability, aimed at sectors that depend on secure lifting, mooring and rigging.

It suits marine operators, ports and industrial businesses that need rigging, mooring or lifting equipment supplied, tested and recertified in one place.

items.description:
Cafe Roux is a restaurant and live music venue at The Farm Village in Noordhoek, serving breakfast from 8:30 to 11am and lunch from midday to 3:30pm daily, with afternoon tea and cakes always available. On select nights the venue opens for dinner alongside live music shows, comedy, films or talks, with additional outdoor seating under a tent for guests attending those events.

The venue publishes a regular what's-on calendar for its live events, which have included musicians taking the stage for an evening show. Reservations for breakfast, lunch and dinner are taken by phone, while event tickets are booked separately through the venue's events contact.

It suits diners who want a daytime meal in Noordhoek as much as visitors looking for an evening of live music or comedy with dinner.

Canterbury House is a bed and breakfast in Bishopscourt, offering four en-suite double rooms and a self-catering cottage. Guests can relax in a large sitting room with an open fireplace and a snooker table, or enjoy a drink at the property's own family pub or out on the patio overlooking the pool and garden.

Rooms include the poolside Garden Room with its own patio, the split-level Tree Room with a private balcony and mountain views, the Canterbury Cottage with a small lounge and kitchenette, and the secluded Protea Room near the tennis court. All rooms are en-suite with TVs, bar fridges and tea and coffee facilities, and wireless internet is available throughout.

The property does not allow smoking or pets, though children are welcome. It suits families and guests who want a quiet, garden-set B&B with a pub and pool in Bishopscourt.

items.description:
Lazari is a cafe in Vredehoek, nestled at the foot of Table Mountain, recently revamped and reopened under new ownership after long standing as a local favourite. The new owner has blended the cafe's retro flair with a fresh, tranquil atmosphere, while keeping much of the original team and the familiar warmth that regulars have always valued.

A talented chef has joined the team to build on the cafe's reputation for scrumptious meals and delectable cakes, with a counter still lined with cakes that invite a browse before ordering. Regulars can still get a well-brewed cafe latte or settle in for a wholesome deli-style meal, whether catching up with friends over breakfast or a relaxed lunch.

It suits Vredehoek locals who want a neighbourhood cafe that has kept its old charm through a change of ownership.

Origin Coffee Roasting runs its flagship cafe at 28 Hudson Street in De Waterkant, roasting coffee from a continent it says was the first to grow and roast it. Alongside the cafe, the business operates a wholesale and roastery arm for trade customers and the African School of Coffee, previously known as Origin Academy, which runs barista and coffee courses.

The De Waterkant cafe serves from early morning on weekdays and a little later on weekends, with its kitchen closing before the cafe itself. Origin's coffee is also served at a range of other venues around the Cape and further afield in South Africa, beyond its own cafe.

It suits coffee lovers who want to visit the roastery's own cafe, train as a barista, or buy coffee wholesale for their own venue.

Quince is a restaurant and deli set inside Little Orchard, a nursery in Diep River, which opened in mid-December 2019. The deli's shelves hold a wide range of jams, preserves and pickles made to stock a pantry, alongside a selection of frozen meals that proved popular even when the restaurant could not seat guests during lockdown.

The restaurant's patio is its prime spot, especially in summer, with dappled shade and a view over the nursery's Little Orchard display, a massive oak tree, and colourful flowering plants. The setting reflects a wider trend of nurseries adding cafes and casual restaurants to their premises, turning a weekend plant-shopping trip into a longer outing.

It suits plant lovers and diners who want a meal with a garden view, or deli items such as preserves to take home.

61 On Camps Bay is a guesthouse at 61 Camps Bay Drive, offering seven rooms split between sea view, luxury sea view and pool view categories. Guests booking are asked for their preferred dates, number of guests and whether they would like a sea view room or a more budget-friendly option.

The guesthouse runs a direct booking offer of 20% off for guests who book through its own website rather than a third-party platform, and it keeps a gallery and guest reviews on its site for visitors deciding between room types. It is positioned in Camps Bay, close to the beach and the suburb's restaurants.

It suits travellers who want a choice of sea view or pool view rooms in Camps Bay, with a discount available for booking directly.

items.description:
Clovelly Country Club is a golf course in the Fish Hoek, or Silvermine, Valley, dating back to 1934 and originally laid out by a designer also responsible for Royal Cape and George golf courses. The layout is routed among sand dunes with the Silvermine River and several ponds coming into play, rewarding accuracy over length on a course of moderate length but tight fairways.

One of the course's best-known holes is the par-four 4th, with a stream and out-of-bounds down the left and a pond guarding the green to sharpen the approach shot. The course has spectacular mountain views and False Bay as a backdrop, and it was reportedly a favourite of golfing great Bobby Locke.

It suits golfers who want a tight, tactical course with coastal and mountain scenery in the Cape Peninsula.
